title: E-mail: Your arrival in Manchester
source: Eigener Übungstext nach dem Aufgabenformat MSA Englisch (Reading: everyday texts)
body:
**From:** Helen Carter

**To:** Jonas Weber

**Subject:** Your arrival on Saturday

Dear Jonas,

(1) We are all looking forward to meeting you next week! (2) I will pick you up at Manchester Piccadilly station on Saturday, 12th July. (3) Your train arrives at 4.15 pm, so please wait at the main entrance near the coffee shop. (4) I will be holding a sign with your name on it. (5) You don't need to bring bed sheets or towels, we have plenty. (6) But do bring a raincoat, it rains a lot here, even in summer! (7) One more thing: my daughter Ellie (14) has a dog called Biscuit. (8) Please let me know if you are allergic to animals. (9) If there is a problem with your train, call me on 07700 900 312.

See you soon,

Helen

title: Note on the fridge
source: Eigener Übungstext nach dem Aufgabenformat MSA Englisch (Reading: everyday texts)
body:
Hi everyone,

(1) Three quick things. (2) The landlord is coming on Monday at 9 am to fix the boiler, so somebody has to be at home. (3) Sam, can you do it? (4) You don't have lectures until 11. (5) Second: please stop leaving your bikes in the hallway. (6) The neighbours have complained twice and I'm tired of being the one who says sorry. (7) And finally, it's Tom's birthday on Friday. (8) I'm going to bake a cake, so if you use the last of the milk, buy a new one! (9) The party starts at 8 pm, bring a friend if you like.

Thanks, Priya

title: Advert: Weekend helpers wanted
source: Eigener Übungstext nach dem Aufgabenformat MSA Englisch (Reading: everyday texts)
body:
**THE GREEN BEAN CAFÉ – WEEKEND HELPERS WANTED**

(1) Do you like people, coffee and a busy kitchen? (2) We are looking for two friendly helpers for Saturdays, 9 am to 3 pm. (3) You will serve drinks, clear tables and help in the kitchen. (4) No experience needed, we will train you in your first week. (5) You must be 16 or older. (6) We pay £8.60 an hour plus tips, and lunch is free. (7) Please e-mail a short CV to jobs@greenbean.co.uk before 30th April. (8) We will invite the best candidates to a short interview in the week after that. (9) Sorry, we cannot answer questions by phone.

subject: EN
title: Reading Part 1: A summer week in Brighton
source: Eigene Übungsaufgabe nach dem Aufgabenformat MSA Englisch (Reading Part 1: Personen zuordnen)
body:
**The people**

- **Leo** (16) is spending a week in Brighton with his class. He loves sport and wants to try something on the water, but he can't swim very well, so it must be safe for beginners.
- **Amara** is a vegetarian and a keen cook. She wants to learn something about local food that she can use at home, and she hates crowds.
- **Mrs Novak** is travelling with her two children (6 and 9). They get bored quickly, so she is looking for something with lots of action where the kids can join in.
- **Dev** is a history student. He is interested in old buildings and wants to see how the kings and queens of the past lived. He doesn't mind stairs.
- **Sophie** wants to relax. She has just finished her exams and is looking for a quiet afternoon with music, but she doesn't want to spend much money.

**The activities**

- **A) Royal Pavilion tour**: Discover the strange palace of King George IV. A two-hour guided tour takes you through the kitchens, the music room and the secret tunnels. Lots of stairs, so wear comfortable shoes.
- **B) Paddleboard lesson for beginners**: Two hours on the calm water of the marina with a trained instructor. Life jackets are provided and you never leave the shallow water. No experience needed.
- **C) Free concerts in Pavilion Gardens**: Every afternoon in August, local bands play in the park. Bring a blanket, sit on the grass and enjoy. Entry is free, drinks cost extra.
- **D) Pier fun fair**: Roller coaster, dodgems and games for the whole family. Children under 10 must be with an adult. Wristband for unlimited rides: £15.
- **E) Vegetarian cooking class**: A small group (maximum six people) cooks a three-course meal with vegetables from the Sussex countryside. You take the recipes home with you.
- **F) Street food market**: Fifty stalls, live DJs and thousands of visitors every Saturday night. Try dishes from all over the world.
- **G) Ghost walk**: A 90-minute evening walk through the old lanes of Brighton with a storyteller who knows every dark secret of the town. Not suitable for small children.

subject: EN
title: Reading Part 1: Courses at the Riverside Youth Centre
source: Eigene Übungsaufgabe nach dem Aufgabenformat MSA Englisch (Reading Part 1: Personen zuordnen)
body:
**The people**

- **Mia** wants to earn some money next summer and needs help with her CV and job interviews.
- **Ben** spends too much time gaming. His parents want him to do something active, but he hates team sports.
- **Layla** loves taking photos with her phone and wants to learn how to make them look more professional.
- **Noah** is shy and gets nervous when he has to speak in front of the class.

**The courses**

- **A) Speak up!**: A friendly four-week course for teenagers who want to feel more confident when talking to a group. Small steps, no pressure.
- **B) Job Ready**: Learn how to write a CV, fill in an application form and answer typical interview questions. Perfect if you are looking for a summer job.
- **C) Five-a-side football**: Every Wednesday evening. Join a team and play in our summer league.
- **D) Phone photography**: Light, angles, editing apps. Bring your own smartphone and turn your snapshots into pictures people will remember.
- **E) Climbing club**: Individual training on our indoor climbing wall. You climb at your own speed, and there is no team and no competition.
- **F) Game design basics**: Build your first simple video game on the computer. No programming knowledge needed.
